text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Appliance maker Electrolux chief executive Michael Treschow says he does not rule out taking over the white goods division of U.S. company Raytheon .
- New European Union drivers licence will have information about country of birth. This is unacceptable, immigrants say.

- Volvo plans to focus on eastern European markets, chief executive Leif Johansson says in an interview. The vehicle maker can survive without merging with another company, he says. Volvo aims to be the world's number one company for busses and trucks. It aims to have an operating margin of five to seven percent over a business cycle for its car division.

- A newspaper survey of 50 stock exchange experts has concluded that Finnish mobile phone company Nokia and car safety equipment maker Autoliv are the best buys around on the Stockholm bourse at the moment. Pharmacueticals major Astra is also considered attractive.
At the other end of the scale, the survey shows it is time to take profits following recent surges in Wallenberg-dominated groups SKF and Electrolux .
